primitives.name: As-of Feature Store
primitives.verbatim_quote: The value is architectural: an append-only bitemporal store keyed by (entity, date) where `get_features(entity, as_of)` strictly filters `date < event_date`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'entity': 'sporting entity identifier (team, pitcher)', 'date': 'timestamp of snapshot', 'as_of': 'reference timestamp for filtering'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are static at time of event; no post-event recomputation allowed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When `date >= event_date`, features become invalid for prediction.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's temporal Bayesian belief update; GSE's state transition on (entity, date) key.

primitives.name: Log5 Pairwise Combiner
primitives.verbatim_quote: **MATH:** Log5 (Bill James): p = (A - A·B)/(A + B - 2AB) — the principled pairwise combiner.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'strength estimate of team A (dimensionless)', 'B': 'strength estimate of team B (dimensionless)', 'p': 'probability of A winning (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Strength estimates are bounded in [0,1]; independent performance models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A or B approaches 0 or 1, p becomes undefined or extreme.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE's pairwise game outcome prediction; GSI's probabilistic strength aggregation.
layer2.telemetry: Match accuracy vs. baseline Elo models.

primitives.name: Differential Feature Assembler
primitives.verbatim_quote: Differential design halves the feature count and matches the binary outcome.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ΔX': 'difference in feature X between teams (unit of X)', 'outcome': 'binary win/loss (0 or 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Binary outcomes align with difference in strength; no noise in differences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When differences collapse to zero, predictive power vanishes.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSE's efficient feature engineering; GSI's reduced-coefficient modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Feature count reduction and model AUC improvement.

The as-of feature store ensures that predictions are made with data available at the time of the event, preventing data leakage. It enforces a strict temporal filter, which is essential for valid time-series modeling. The Log5 combiner provides a principled way to combine two strength estimates into a probability of one team beating another, assuming independence and bounded strength values. The differential feature assembler reduces dimensionality by focusing on differences rather than absolute values, improving model efficiency and reducing overfitting. These primitives together support robust, scalable forecasting in MLB where season-long trends must be disentangled from point-in-time dynamics.
